text:
Maria Ramos: Heads-up — after the batching refactor merged yesterday I see a small but steady perf regression on mixed-packing workloads, especially on A10 clusters. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/boards/packing-regressions :eyes:
Kevin Li: ack, can you paste the profile that shows the regression?
Maria Ramos: quick snippet from the perf trace (p99 latency + tail tokens):
```
model: llama-2-13b (q4)
hw: a10-rtx
before-refactor p99: 112ms
after-refactor p99: 138ms
KV hit rate: 72% -> 68%
batch tokens avg: 640 -> 730
kernel-switches/sec: +18%
```
Josh Patel: interesting — batch tokens increased which could push kernel selector into a different path. Did we change the slice-formation gating?
Maria Ramos: yes, the gating now favors larger batches when queue depth variance is low. That changed token-budget targets per slot.
Anna Gomez: could be we pushed some L4/A100 devices into a kernel that is slower for mid-length sequences. I saw similar in last year's kernel-fit matrix.
Kevin Li: can you run a micro-profiling run that pins same request mix across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 and capture kernel id counts + KV fragmentation? Use the test harness `tools/batchprobe --fixed-seed --slot-target=650`.
Maria Ramos: running now. attaching short log output when ready.
perfbot: job 98431 queued on a10-rtx-3 (ETA ~2m)
Maria Ramos: results (summarized):
```
A10: avg p99 140ms, kernel#7 54%, kernel#9 31%, kv-frag=0.15
T4: avg p99 125ms, kernel#4 68%, kernel#7 12%, kv-frag=0.12
L4: avg p99 118ms, kernel#11 60%, kernel#7 25%, kv-frag=0.18
A100: avg p99 110ms, kernel#2 82%, kernel#7 4%, kv-frag=0.05
H100: avg p99 105ms, kernel#2 88%, kernel#7 3%, kv-frag=0.04
```
Josh Patel: kernel#7 looks like the new tiled-attn path that has high setup overhead but better throughput at >1k tokens. If our batches grew into that region, p99 could worsen for short/medium sequences.
Kevin Li: KV fragmentation higher on L4 and A10 — that would reduce hit-rate and force recompute. Is fragmentation correlated with batch token distribution?
Maria Ramos: yeah, we saw a small right-shift in token distribution after the gating tweak. More medium-length requests got coalesced rather than staying in smaller slots.
Anna Gomez: proposal: tighten slot token-budget target for A10/T4 to 600 tokens and lower L4 threshold to 580 to keep kernel selector on the low-latency kernels for our typical 200–800 token mix. Meanwhile let A100/H100 keep higher targets.
Josh Patel: +1. We should also add a short-circuit: if KV hit rate drops below 70% for consecutive 30s, force fall-back to conservative slot sizing for that cardclass.
Kevin Li: agree. That circuit-breaker would prevent slow drift. Also log a metric `batch.kv_frag_change` to alert on sudden fragmentation jumps.
Maria Ramos: I'll open a PR with the slot-target overrides and the KV circuit-breaker. Quick benchmark plan: run 30m stable load with random seeds across card classes and verify p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, kernel-switch counts.
perfbot: PR #4820 created by maria — https://git.redwood/pulls/4820 (slot-target overrides + kv breaker) :white_check_mark:
Anna Gomez: remember to include a canary rollout: 5% of traffic for 1h then 25% for 2h before full roll.
Josh Patel: also add synthetic repro that reproduces the shift so we can run regression tests in CI.
Maria Ramos: noted. I'll add the harness and runbench. Thanks all — will post results here once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
Kevin Li: thanks — and add a per-cardclass dashboard panel for kernel-id distribution so we can detect mode shifts earlier.
Maria Ramos: added to the dashboard board (view-only link): https://dash.redwood/internal/boards/kernel-id-tracking
perfbot: canary rollout started on a10-rtx (5% traffic)
Maria Ramos: canary p99 looks 6ms better than before after forcing slot-target 600 on a10-rtx-3. I'll wait for 30m baseline.
Anna Gomez: great — if this holds we should bake these cardclass targets into the kernel selection table and document the rationale in the runtime playbook.
Maria Ramos: filing that doc now under eng-runtime/ops-playbook. Action items: 1) PR #4820 (Maria) 2) Canary metrics review (All) 3) CI repro + regression test (Josh) 4) Dashboard panels (Kevin)
Kevin Li: tagging follow-up owners in the PR.
Josh Patel: will draft the CI test today.
Maria Ramos: closing loop — early canary looks promising, will update after full rollout.
